To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

new digital media have reshaped traditional media in ways that have made it easier for elites to control the political content of the media, even if the control is somewhat different in different countries, and that elites have been able to use digital media to shape consumer culture in similar ways in the four countries.

digital media have reshaped, but not replaced, traditional media and that the relation between elites, political and cultural, and people has been transformed, but not eliminated, in a variety of ways.
digital media are not changing the relation between elites, media, and people, but that they are reshaping it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social consequences of the development and diffusion of digital media and how these consequences are shaped by the political, economic, and cultural context of different societies.
the social implications of the use of media, in particular digital media, in the four countries mentioned above, and with how the relation between media, elites, and people is changing.
the question of whether and if so how the digital divide is being reshaped by digital technologies and social networking media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
digital media have not yet changed the basic Weberian pattern of the relation between elites, media, and people.
the digital divide is a global reality, and the digital divide is still a reality.
new media, while reshaping the relation between elites in some respects, do not fundamentally alter this relation, which continues to be one of asymmetry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relation between elites, media, and people has been shaped by digital media, but that this relation is still very different from one country to another.
the digital divides are not so much about the availability of digital technology, but about the uses of this technology.
the digital divide is not only about technology but also about social relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in terms of politics, the digital divide between elites and people continues to exist, even if the relation between elites is reshaped by the new media.
digital media are reshaping the relation between elites, people, and culture, but that these changes are quite different from one country to the next.

the relation between elites, media, and people is shaped in different ways in different countries, and that this relation is not simply a matter of technology, but also of the social and cultural contexts in which technology is deployed.
